title: Hypertension Management: Current Guideline Updates and Therapeutic Sequencing
summary: Contemporary guidance emphasizes accurate diagnosis, earlier combination therapy, and outcome‑driven sequencing anchored in compelling indications. High‑quality trials support thiazide‑like diuretics, ACEi/ARB, and CCB as first‑line; beta‑blockers are reserved for specific indications. SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP‑1 RAs confer BP‑lowering and CV–renal benefit in comorbid diabetes/HF. Resistant hypertension requires structured evaluation, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and consideration of device therapy.
clinicalQuestion: What is the optimal, evidence‑based approach to diagnosing, initiating, and sequencing antihypertensive therapy in adults, integrating recent guideline updates and major trial data?

heroStats.label: BP Targets
heroStats.value: <130/80 mmHg for most; individualized in frailty/CKD

heroStats.label: Initial combo
heroStats.value: 2 drugs if BP ≥20/10 mmHg above goal

keyMoments.title: Single‑pill combinations first
keyMoments.body: Initiate dual therapy for stage 2 hypertension to improve speed to control and adherence; prefer single‑pill ACEi/ARB + CCB or thiazide‑like combinations.

keyMoments.title: Outcome‑anchored choices
keyMoments.body: Use chlorthalidone or indapamide over HCTZ; ACEi/ARB for CKD/proteinuria; add SGLT2i in T2D/HF for cardiorenal benefit.

keyMoments.title: Resistant hypertension playbook
keyMoments.body: Confirm adherence and out‑of‑office BP; add spironolactone; evaluate secondary causes; consider renal denervation in selected patients.

keyMoments.title: Lower is better—safely
keyMoments.body: Intensive SBP targeting reduces MACE and mortality, with careful monitoring for hypotension and AKI risk.

sections.title: Confirm the Diagnosis and Set Individualized Targets
sections.blurb: Use accurate measurements and out‑of‑office monitoring; target <130/80 mmHg for most adults, balancing benefit and risk.

steps.title: Standardize measurement
steps.body: Use validated devices, 5‑minute rest, appropriate cuff, and average ≥2 readings; confirm with home or ambulatory BP to detect white coat or masked HTN.

steps.title: Set targets informed by evidence
steps.body: For non‑diabetic adults at elevated risk, intensive SBP <120 mmHg reduced MACE and all‑cause mortality (SPRINT: **HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.64–0.89**), with higher hypotension/syncope/AKI risk [1]. In diabetes, ACCORD BP showed neutral primary outcome but less stroke with intensive SBP (**HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.39–0.89**) at cost of adverse events [2].

steps.title: Lifestyle as foundation
steps.body: Weight loss, sodium <1.5–2 g/day, DASH diet, alcohol moderation, and physical activity yield additive BP reductions; sustain alongside pharmacotherapy.

sections.title: Start Right: First‑Line and Stepwise Intensification
sections.blurb: Prioritize agents with proven outcome benefits and use single‑pill combinations to accelerate control.

steps.title: Select first‑line classes
steps.body: Thiazide‑like diuretic (chlorthalidone or indapamide), ACE inhibitor or ARB, and dihydropyridine CCB have the strongest outcome data. Prefer thiazide‑like over HCTZ; ALLHAT favored chlorthalidone for HF prevention [3].

steps.title: Initiate dual therapy for stage 2
steps.body: If ≥20/10 mmHg above goal, start single‑pill ACEi/ARB + CCB or ACEi/ARB + thiazide‑like; combination improves adherence and BP lowering. Avoid ACEi + ARB together.

steps.title: Compelling indications guide class choice
steps.body: CKD with albuminuria: ACEi/ARB slow kidney disease progression (e.g., RENAAL: **RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.73–0.96**; IDNT: **RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66–0.97**) [4], [5]. CAD/post‑MI/HFrEF: use beta‑blocker and ACEi/ARB; add MRA in HFrEF. Black adults without CKD/heart failure: initiate thiazide‑like or CCB as per outcomes data.

steps.title: Add‑on agents by phenotype
steps.body: Resistant HTN: add spironolactone (PATHWAY‑2: **placebo‑adjusted SBP −8.7 mmHg** vs doxazosin/bisoprolol) [6]. Diabetes or CKD: add SGLT2 inhibitor—lowers BP ~3–5 mmHg and reduces CV/renal events (EMPA‑REG, CANVAS, DAPA‑CKD) [7], [8], [9]. Obesity: GLP‑1 RA produces additional BP lowering and CV benefit (SELECT: **HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.72–0.90**) [10].

steps.title: When to consider procedures
steps.body: In true resistant HTN despite optimized triple therapy plus MRA and confirmed adherence, catheter‑based renal denervation lowers ambulatory SBP (SPYRAL HTN‑OFF MED Pivotal: **−4.0 to −6.0 mmHg**) with favorable safety [11].

sections.title: Class Priorities, Doses, and Monitoring
sections.blurb: Use outcome‑proven agents; up‑titrate every 4–6 weeks while monitoring labs and adverse effects.

cards.title: First‑line agents
items: Thiazide‑like diuretic: chlorthalidone 12.5–25 mg qAM; monitor Na/K; superior HF prevention vs amlodipine/lisinopril in ALLHAT [3].
ACE inhibitor: lisinopril 10–40 mg qd; monitor K/Cr; avoid in pregnancy; start lower in CKD/elderly.
ARB: losartan 50–100 mg qd; monitor K/Cr; preferable if ACEi cough/angioedema.
DHP‑CCB: amlodipine 5–10 mg qd; monitor edema; neutral on electrolytes.

cards.title: Avoid or use with caution
items: Do not combine ACEi + ARB due to AKI/hyperkalemia without outcome gain.
Minoxidil/hydralazine as later‑line with beta‑blocker + loop diuretic if needed.
Beta‑blockers not first‑line for uncomplicated HTN; prioritize when CAD, arrhythmia, or HFrEF present.

cards.title: Resistant hypertension protocol
items: Confirm home/ABPM and adherence; review NSAIDs, OCPs, decongestants.
Ensure triple therapy: ACEi/ARB + CCB + thiazide‑like (prefer chlorthalidone or indapamide).
Add spironolactone 12.5–25 mg (monitor K/Cr); consider eplerenone if gynecomastia [6].
Screen secondary causes: primary aldosteronism, OSA, renal artery stenosis, CKD, pheochromocytoma, Cushing.
Consider renal denervation in selected patients with persistent uncontrolled BP [11].

cards.title: Comorbid condition tailoring
items: CKD with albuminuria: ACEi/ARB first; add SGLT2 inhibitor for renal/CV protection (DAPA‑CKD: **HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.51–0.72**) [9].
Type 2 diabetes with ASCVD: GLP‑1 RA with CV benefit (SELECT semaglutide: **HR 0.80**) plus SGLT2i as indicated [10].
HFrEF: ACEi/ARB/ARNI + beta‑blocker + MRA + SGLT2i; thiazide‑like or loop diuretic as needed for BP/volume.

cards.title: Follow‑up and monitoring
items: Reassess BP and adverse effects every 4–6 weeks until control, then every 3–6 months.
Check BMP 1–2 weeks after starting or titrating ACEi/ARB/MRA; monitor Na/K with thiazide‑like diuretics.
Encourage home BP logs; adjust for orthostatic symptoms, especially in older adults or with intensive targets.
